clue.text: Sweet, one jammed in cake hole?

blocks.note: first meaning: a large hard round candy
second meaning, read literally: something that blocks a mouth

explanation.walkthrough: Cake hole and gob are both British slang for the mouth, so the second half describes the sweet's name taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A gobstopper is a big hard candy, named because it fills the mouth (gob is slang for mouth).

clue.text: Well, sling your hook and shut your mouth!

blocks.note: 'sling your hook' is British slang for go away
the exclamation telling someone to be quiet

explanation.surface: A rude dismissal: clear off and be quiet!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well' looks like the start of a speech but it is the definition, an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild interjections expressing surprise, so one can stand in for the other.

clue.text: Rail man in loco

blocks.note: a man, i.e. a piece, in chess

explanation.surface: A railwayman working on a locomotive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loco' looks like short for locomotive, fitting the railway picture, but it is the slang adjective for crazy.
explanation.definitionFit: Barking (short for barking mad) is British slang for insane, the same as the American slang loco.

clue.text: Cash for example I spread out, splitting money

indicators.note: to split something is to break into it, so these words go inside the word for money

blocks.note: to splay is to spread out

explanation.surface: Someone sharing out money, with cash as the example.
explanation.walkthrough: Pat Cash is the Australian who won Wimbledon in 1987; the capital C is disguised at the start of the clue. A tenner is a ten-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: Pat Cash is a famous example of a professional in the racket sport, so he exemplifies the answer.

clue.text: Utopian scene cut, commercial is screened

indicators.note: something screened is shut off behind a covering, so the inner words sit within the outer one

blocks.note: to pare is to trim or cut

explanation.surface: A TV editor cutting a scene of an ideal world and showing an advert instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Paradise is a perfect place, the kind of idealised setting a utopia describes.

clue.text: Register I sent off, fifty in it

indicators.note: something gone off has gone bad or awry, so these letters are rearranged
'in it' places the extra letter inside the rearranged group just made

blocks.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone posting off a registration form with fifty pounds enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlist is to sign up or enrol, which is what registering for something means.

clue.text: Socialist quit

blocks.note: first meaning: on the political ... wing
second meaning: past tense of leave

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a socialist resigning; the two words are separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: Left describes the socialist wing of politics, and is also the past tense of leave, which matches quit.

clue.text: Food that's cracked along with nut for academic

explanation.surface: Cracked nuts and food handed out, perhaps to a scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nut' looks like more food alongside the egg, but here it is slang for the head.
explanation.definitionFit: An egghead is an informal name for an intellectual or scholarly person.

clue.text: Entertaining current bishop, drops childhood friends?

indicators.note: to entertain is to host guests, so the outer word takes the others in

blocks.note: an eddy is a swirling current
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop being entertained and then dropping old friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Teddy bears are cuddly toys that children treat as companions, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Bound to need bowl for Chinese food

blocks.note: to bowl a ball is to roll it along

explanation.surface: Someone certain to want a bowl for their Chinese takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'certain to', but 'Bound' is a verb meaning leap and 'bowl' is a verb too.
explanation.definitionFit: A spring roll is a fried pancake roll with a vegetable filling, a staple of Chinese cuisine.

clue.text: Pensionable artist cut back

indicators.note: cut means trimmed short, so the painter's name loses its final letter
going back means reading the letters from right to left

blocks.note: Edgar Degas, the French Impressionist painter

explanation.surface: An elderly artist having his pension cut back.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone pensionable has reached retirement age, so they are old.

clue.text: Spaniards go abroad under British travel permit

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or all over the place, so the letters wander out of order
in a down clue, being under something means coming after it in the answer

explanation.surface: Spanish travellers heading overseas below some British ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A boarding pass is the document that permits a passenger to get on a plane or ship.

clue.text: Reportedly vital, little bird?

indicators.note: reportedly means as spoken by someone, so these words count for how they are pronounced

explanation.surface: Talk of a small bird being essential.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the answer is also a New Zealander, as well as the flightless bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The kiwi is a flightless New Zealand bird, and its name is also slang for a New Zealander.

clue.text: Find type of music so

blocks.note: so, as in 'so good', means very

explanation.surface: Someone stumbling upon a kind of music they like, so much.
explanation.definitionFit: A discovery is a noun for something found, the same as the noun find.

clue.text: It appears when old, judiciously saving time

indicators.note: saving something means keeping it safe within, so one word holds another

explanation.surface: An old person carefully putting time aside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It appears' is a clause standing for an adverb: 'ostensibly' means apparently, as it appears.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostensibly means apparently or seemingly, describing what seems to be the case on the surface.

clue.text: Initial letters for guide

blocks.note: to initial a document is to sign it

explanation.surface: Opening letters of words used as a guide, like an acronym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initial letters' looks like first letters of words, but 'Initial' is a verb and 'letters' means mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A signpost points travellers the right way, so it acts as a guide.

clue.text: Check line hidden by blusher?

indicators.note: something kept out of sight by another is covered by it, so one goes within the other

blocks.note: a blushing bride is the stock phrase, so a bride is a blusher

explanation.surface: Checking for a line of make-up concealed under blusher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blusher' wants to be make-up; the question mark marks it as one who blushes, the blushing bride.
explanation.definitionFit: To bridle is to restrain or curb, as a horse is held back by its bridle, so it means check.

clue.text: Children's game, climax sounds a hoot!

indicators.note: sounds means the way it is pronounced, so the first word counts for its spoken form

blocks.note: the peak is the high point
a hoot of derision, a boo

explanation.surface: The high point of a children's game being hilarious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a hoot' reads as 'great fun', but hoot is the jeer.
explanation.definitionFit: Peekaboo is the game of hiding the face and revealing it to amuse a baby.

clue.text: Reel in tangled net, minor blow

indicators.note: a tangled thing is twisted into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a rap is a light knock

explanation.surface: An angler hauling in a catch caught in a snarled net, with a little knock.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel in, figuratively, is to lure and catch someone, which is what ensnaring does.

clue.text: A hint of water soaked up by matter in liquefaction

indicators.note: a hint of something is just a trace, so only its opening letter is used
soaked up means absorbed, so these letters end up within the outer word

explanation.surface: A drop of water being absorbed by a substance as it melts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' does double duty in the surface but contributes its own letter before the hint of water.
explanation.definitionFit: Thawing is the process of melting ice into water, a kind of becoming liquid.

clue.text: Participant in conflict has to admire cunning

indicators.note: cunning means crafty or artful, so these letters are craftily rearranged

explanation.surface: A combatant forced to respect an opponent's guile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Participant in conflict' suggests a fighter, but the answer takes part as a go-between.
explanation.definitionFit: A mediator is involved in a dispute as the neutral party trying to settle it, so is a participant.

clue.text: Audiobook's plot followed

indicators.note: audio means relating to sound, so the next words count for how they are spoken

blocks.note: a tract is a short book or pamphlet, and also a plot or stretch of land; the leading audio signals that it is heard, not seen

explanation.surface: The storyline of a recorded book being kept up with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Audiobook' looks like one word but splits as a sound signal plus 'book', and 'book's plot' means book is plot: both are tract.
explanation.definitionFit: To track someone is to follow their trail, so tracked means followed.

clue.text: Bishop of Rome accompanying you is a muscular, tattooed character

blocks.note: the Pope is the Bishop of Rome

explanation.surface: The Pope standing alongside you, as a brawny tattooed figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Popeye the Sailor is the cartoon character with huge forearms and an anchor tattoo, strengthened by spinach.

clue.text: Digging foundations?

blocks.note: surface reading: excavating the base of a building
setter's reading: the groundwork or preparation for a project, done literally with a digging tool

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a builder's job description; the answer is the idiom for preliminary hard work, which is also literally work with a spade.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the tedious preparatory labour that lays the groundwork for something later.

clue.text: Damsel cut by old object

indicators.note: being cut by something means being split open with it in the middle

explanation.surface: A maiden wounded by an ancient item.
explanation.definitionFit: An object in the sense of aim or purpose is a goal, something one strives for.

clue.text: Light up part of rest area

indicators.note: part of means only a portion is wanted, sitting inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Illuminating a section of a motorway lay-by.
explanation.definitionFit: A star is a light in the night sky, one of the heavenly lights.

clue.text: Margin on boater at the front?

definitions.text: Margin on boater at the front?

indicators.note: at the front points to the leading letter of the word just before

blocks.note: a rim is an edge or margin

explanation.surface: The edge of a straw hat sticking out over the forehead.
explanation.walkthrough: A boater is a flat-topped straw hat, so the whole clue also describes the answer: its projecting edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The brim of a hat is the projecting edge around it, which on a boater juts out at the front.

clue.text: Drag fire extinguisher, possibly?

blocks.note: first meaning: a bore, someone who spoils the fun
second meaning, literal: a damp cover that smothers flames

explanation.walkthrough: 'Drag' is the slang noun for a tedious person; the second half reads the idiom literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A wet blanket dampens enthusiasm, a killjoy, and a soaked blanket could literally smother a fire.

clue.text: System of exercises key to understanding Rigveda, last of all

indicators.note: last of all means the final letter of every one of the words is taken

blocks.note: the final letters of each of these four words

explanation.surface: An exercise regime said to unlock an ancient Hindu scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rigveda is the oldest Hindu sacred text, a fitting scene for a practice of Indian origin.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoga is a Hindu discipline of postures and breathing practised as physical exercise.

clue.text: Again take a look at order, since fraudulent

indicators.note: fraudulent means fake or crooked, so these letters are bent out of order

explanation.surface: Reviewing an instruction because it turns out to be a con.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconsider is to think about something afresh, reviewing a decision a second time.
